concepts.hook: *Tiskel* — "the one that went down": an eel that swam south to spawn and never came back up, so its lamp burns in the Unflown where no net reaches.
A nanny goat stepped off the cliff-edge during a midsummer feast and kept walking on nothing, and her hoofprints are the faint stars the children count.
*Halvi* — "the Stayer": a seal left on a drifting floe that turns its head northward forever, watching for the islands it can no longer reach.
A shark whose dorsal fin was cut into a sail by a drowned boatwright, now hunting the shadows of ships that were never built.
A grey heron that stands on nothing and fishes the drift of cloud, and it only appears to sailors who are lost and have stopped calling out.
*Mirath* — "the Hollow Throat": a tern that carries the names of the drowned in its gullet and drops them into the wrong sea, so the dead are never where their families look.
A flightless bird whose single egg rolled off a ledge in a gale, and she still sits on the cold rock every night, counting the lamps she thinks are her egg.
A cormorant spreads its wings on a dead rock in the Unflown, the way the islanders hang nets, because the drowned are told to dry before they go aloft.
A storm-petrel so light it once pattered across the water to a boat in distress, and its footprints are a line of small stars that lead nowhere.
A squid with eight arms wrapped around a sunken boat's lantern, holding it up to the surface for a crew that never saw it.
A deep-sea fish with a light hung on a stalk above its head, which lured a foolish girl down into the dark, and the lamp is still tempting people from the Unflown.
A drowned jellyfish whose bell rings faintly whenever someone dies on the islands, so the Ilvari say it is the first thing to know of a death.
A sea-cow with one long tusk who sang deep through the water so that the sailors heard the wind's hum, and her song is still the sound of very far weather.
A crab that walks the underside of the Unflown, scraping at the edges of the sky for things that fell out of Vel, and it never gives back what it finds.
A manta ray with wings of cloth-coloured skin that carries rope ends and oar-pins across the dark, delivering the gear of boats that will not come home.
A storm of glowing plankton that pulses in the far south, and the Ilvari say each pulse is a drowned person breathing out their last light.
A kelp-woman who married a fisherman on a hot calm day and grew her stalk up through the sky after he was lost, and her long brown fronds still sway in the Unflown.
A tree of wrack logs that floats with no roots, and the islanders will not burn its wood, because a fire of it would bring the drowned back smelling of salt.
A thistle of ice that blooms only in the coldest dark of the Unflown, and its seed heads are said to be the ice-lamps the lost use to find their way.
A coil of bladderwrack and old rope that moves in the swell like a serpent and ate the net of a boatwright who tried to pull it out of the sea.
A grey hound made of falling weather that runs through the Unflown after a lost lamb, and when it barks, the rain begins somewhere in the islands.
A mare of hail with no hooves who gallops over the drift-ice, and she is the reason the Ilvari keep a bone whistle tied to every lamp.
A gull of the Calm who has hung motionless for a thousand years so that no wind can reach the drowned, and sailors say its silence is the stillness that drowns the living.
A waterspout that spins like a woman drawing up a net, and dancers on the islands copy her turns to ask the Unflown for a safe return.
A great white tooth that Tavo the Gale lost biting a rigging-line in a fury, lodged in the Unflown, and no one who takes it can give it back.
A worm the length of a fjord that lives under the far ice, lifting its blind head through the sky-floor when the ice cracks, and the cracks are the Ilvari's oldest warning.
A young sea-calf who would not follow her mother down into the deep water and wandered out through the Leeward sea into the Unflown, and she still cries in a voice like a child.
A ram that fell from a sea-stack chasing a goat and now stands on the wave-tops with its horns in the cloud, a warning to climbers not to follow their animals.
A hollow reed the wind plays through in the Unflown, and the Ilvari hear its note at a funeral and say it is the voice of someone who died without a song.
*Ranu* — "the Dry Wings": a sea-moth that circles every drowned lamp in the Unflown until its wings burn to ash, and the ash falls back down as salt on the islands.
A sea-rope knot that Aun tied in the first days and never completed, so the Unflown has one loose loop still waiting for a hand to finish it, and that is why things go missing.
